resources.string: The app checks once a day when you open it. It never checks in the background.
Asking for the newest release of %1$s.
Nothing to download. Checked just now.
Newer than the %1$s you are running.
Add a read-only token and updates carry on by themselves.
Not set — updates cannot be checked
No token yet, so there\'s nothing to check with.
The saved token couldn\'t be read on this phone.
It\'s still saved. Open the token screen to see why, and whether to wait or paste a new one.
Saved, but couldn\'t be read — open to see why
Your token has expired or been revoked — GitHub accepted it before and doesn\'t now. Paste a new one and updates will carry on.
Google Play has nothing newer on the test track.
Google Play will download and install it, then reopen the app.
Google Play has it, but won\'t let the app install it from here. Open the Play Store to update.
An update is already being installed.
Google Play is applying it. It finishes on its own.
That is not the same as being up to date. Check that the Play Store is signed in, and try again.
Nothing was changed. Try again when you have a connection.
This build didn\'t come from Google Play.

Updates now arrive through Google Play, and only a copy installed from there receives them. This one also won\'t appear in Android Auto \u2014 the car only runs apps the Play Store installed. Install from the test track to get both back.
Downloaded. Android will ask you to confirm the install.
The update is downloaded and ready whenever you are.
Android needs your permission for this app to install apps. It only asks once.
That release has no .apk attached, so there\'s nothing to install.
The download stopped before it finished. Nothing was installed — try again.
The download didn\'t arrive intact, so it wasn\'t installed. Try again.
Not enough space for the update — it needs %1$s. Free some up and try again.
There\'s a newer release, but its version tag isn\'t one this app can read.

Updates for this app come from its own GitHub repository, %1$s, which is private — so it needs a read-only token for that one repository, stored encrypted on this phone and sent to github.com and nowhere else.

github.com → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens.

Repository access: only this repository.
Permissions: Contents → Read-only.

Nothing else is needed.
GitHub didn\'t accept that token. If it\'s one you made a while ago it may have expired — they do that. Make a new one and paste it again.
That token works, but it can\'t see %1$s. Check it\'s from the account that owns the repository, and that this repository is selected.
That token can see the repository but not its releases. It needs Contents: Read-only.
GitHub is rate-limiting this token. Try again after %1$s.
GitHub is rate-limiting this token. Try again in a little while.
Can\'t reach GitHub. Check your connection and try again.
GitHub returned an error (%1$d). Try again in a bit.
The saved token can\'t be read on this phone any more. It\'s kept, but the key that opened it is gone — paste a new one, or remove it.
The saved token couldn\'t be read just now. It\'s kept — this usually clears after an unlock or a restart. If it doesn\'t, paste a new one.
That token is good, but this phone wouldn\'t store it. Try again - and if it keeps happening, restart the phone and paste it once more.
What you can reach from this network
Can I reach my homelab from here
Remote addresses only. Nothing here logs in.
Nothing answered, and all %1$d failed in the same way. That points at this network rather than at your services.
Nothing answered, and they failed in different ways — so there is no single explanation.
Your router answered every one of these, but nothing is serving them. The connection is fine; the services behind it are not running or not being proxied.
It asked who you are, which means you reached it.
It sent you to its login page, which means you reached it.
Something answered and it was not what this address expects. Worth opening to see.
You reached your router, but nothing is being served for this name. The network is fine — check the service is running and that the proxy rule still exists.
Your router answered and the service behind it did not. Nothing is filtering you: this one is at home.
You reached it and it is unhappy. That is a problem at home, not on this network.
This network\'s DNS gave no address for it. Often the first place a filtered network interferes.
Something answered the connection and rejected it outright.
The address resolved and the connection never opened. The port is blocked, or nothing is listening.
Either something is intercepting this connection, or the certificate has expired — the phone cannot tell which. Check the certificate\'s date.
Nothing is intercepting you — the certificate simply lapsed and needs renewing.
The connection opened and then the encrypted handshake did not finish. That is what a network blocking by site name looks like.
Something went wrong that this app does not have a name for. Worth reporting with a screenshot.
These %1$d have no remote address, so nothing can be said about them from here.
Read each pane through its zmx daemon (history --vt) so colours and bold reach the phone. Needs Live sessions on in agterm; a pane without a daemon shows plain text as before.

Pair this phone with your laptop to reach your terminal sessions from it. On the laptop, run bridgecert qr — it saves a pairing code to your Desktop. Open the image, then scan it with this phone or send it over and choose the file.
Without camera access this app cannot read the code from your laptop\'s screen. You can still pair by choosing the image file.
That image is not a pairing code. Scan again, or choose a different image.
Point at the code on your laptop
Hold the phone steady. It reads the code by itself — there is nothing to press.
Still nothing. Try moving closer, or steadying the phone — or choose the image file instead.
Check both against your laptop. The fingerprint says the code came from your laptop; the address says where this phone will look for it, and it is the one that can be wrong. If either differs, stop.
This phone\'s key will stop working on its own

It was made in a way that expires when the phone locks, which is what kept breaking your connection. A new key fixes that for good. The cost: your laptop will stop recognising this phone until you send it the new certificate and pin it, exactly as you did when you first paired. The fingerprint below is the one your laptop trusts right now.
Make a new key and pair again
This phone\'s key will not sign

The key that proves who this phone is has stopped working, so the laptop will refuse it. A new key fixes that, and it ends the current pairing: your laptop trusts the fingerprint below and will not trust the new one until you pin it there. Nothing else on this phone changes.
Make a new key and pair again
This phone has no screen lock
The key that proves who this phone is can only exist on a phone that locks. Set a PIN, pattern or password in Settings, then come back and pair. This app cannot set one for you.
Your laptop does not know this phone yet
The laptop is stored on this phone. Now the laptop needs this phone\'s certificate, or it will refuse the connection. Send it while you are still sitting at the laptop.
bridgecert prints a fingerprint when it pins. It must match this one — if it does not, it pinned a different file.
I have pinned it on the laptop

This phone holds its own key, generated on the device and never shared. You have sent its certificate to the laptop. Whether the laptop accepted it is something only the laptop knows — your sessions appearing under Terminal is the proof.
Your terminal sessions on the laptop
No sessions are open on your laptop.
This is not the laptop you paired with. The certificate it presented is a different one. Pair again to trust it.
The paired laptop\'s certificate has expired. Create a new one on the laptop, then pair again.
Line breaks would each press Return. Your text is still here.
Your laptop will not type that. Your text is still here.
Your laptop would not take that file. Your text is still here.
Send files to your laptop and put their paths in the box
Its path is in the box — press Enter when you are ready.
Your laptop took it and the screen did not change — that is normal for a password prompt or a command still running.
That did not reach your laptop.

Arrow keys may behave oddly inside full-screen programs like vim or less. This app cannot tell which mode a program has put the terminal in, so it always sends the ordinary form. It is a limit, not a bug being worked on.
More keys: arrows, backspace, line editing
Hide the arrows and line-editing keys
Width control: waiting for the terminal to be measured
Your laptop has not said if the fit is on. Press Fit to measure again.
Showing the left pane. Switch to the right one, opening it on your laptop if there is none.
Showing the right pane. Switch to the left one.
%1$d columns. Hold Fit to measure again.
Fitted to this phone. Hold Fit to measure again.
Laptop keeps its own width. Hold Fit to measure again.
Waiting for your laptop to answer again.
Output resumed from where it stopped.
Your laptop did not confirm it. Nothing was added.
Your laptop did not confirm it. The name is unchanged.
A name cannot contain a control character.
Your laptop did not confirm it. Nothing was removed.
Your laptop did not open the second pane.
Your laptop could not work out the width this time. Your window is as it was.
This session is a different shape. Press Fit to measure it.
Fit the laptop\'s terminal to this phone, %1$d columns
Put the laptop\'s window back; it is fitted to %1$d columns
This phone\'s key can no longer prove who it is, so your laptop has nothing to check. Open pairing to make a new key.
Something in here is waiting on you
Disconnected. Nothing is connected to your laptop.
No laptop is paired with this phone yet.
Your laptop is not answering. This app cannot tell why from here.
Your router answered, but nothing was listening behind it.
Your laptop did not answer in time.
This app fell behind the stream and closed the connection. Nothing is wrong with your laptop.
Your laptop answered with something this app did not understand.
Your laptop answered, but could not list your sessions.
Say it, or type it when parked
Done keeps the line. Enter sends it.
Press Fit to measure this width
This phone has no speech recogniser
The microphone was not allowed. Allow it on the phone.
Sent. The laptop showed no output.
Your laptop refused what was sent. The words are back in the band.
Update the bridge on the Mac
Laptop unreachable · tap and hold to retry
